title: Myanmar social-media and hate-speech context
system_purpose: Social platform distribution and communication in a conflict-affected information environment
decision_impact: Visibility and circulation of public speech and information
affected_groups: Rohingya and other affected communities; social-media users; public institutions
verified_facts: The UN fact-finding mission examined hate speech and serious human-rights violations in Myanmar, including the surrounding role of social media in the information environment.
reported_harm: The report documents severe human-rights harms in the conflict and supports treating local context, hate speech, and distribution mechanisms as safety-critical; it does not isolate a single technical causal mechanism.
quantitative_evidence: The report does not provide a product-comparable denominator for algorithmic harm rates.
limitations: The conflict has many causes and actors; the source cannot quantify causal contribution of a particular ranking or assistant.

title: UK ICO political-data analytics investigation
system_purpose: Political campaign data analytics and targeting
decision_impact: Use of personal data to target political communications
affected_groups: Voters; social-media users; political campaign subjects
verified_facts: The UK ICO conducted a formal investigation into data analytics in political campaigns, including concerns involving Facebook-derived personal data and targeting.
reported_harm: Potentially opaque collection and use of political or social data can undermine privacy, autonomy, and trust in democratic communication.
quantitative_evidence: The ICO report describes an investigation rather than a single causal estimate of voter influence.
limitations: The historic UK investigation does not determine behavior or legal obligations for a fixed-corpus Vietnamese research prototype.

title: Cambodian Prime Minister moderation decision
decision_impact: Whether a high-reach political video remains available or is removed
affected_groups: Political opponents; platform users; Cambodian public; journalists
verified_facts: The Oversight Board found that a video with threats against political opponents violated Meta's violence policy and required removal, reversing Meta's prior decision to leave it up.
reported_harm: Leaving threatening political speech available can increase risk of intimidation or violence; over-removal can also impair public access to information, so context and proportionality matter.
quantitative_evidence: The decision does not supply a population-level rate of harm or prove downstream violence from the item.
limitations: These are platform-policy decisions and do not replace country-specific legal, linguistic, or safety assessment.
